summary: Created local administrator account `opsadmin` on node1 with a private home directory (`drwx------`) and full administrative privileges via the `wheel` group. Node1 was restarted and the account persisted correctly across the reboot.
actions_performed: Created user account `opsadmin` with `useradd -m -s /bin/bash -G wheel opsadmin`
Set home directory permissions to 700 (private) with `chmod 700 /home/opsadmin`
Verified wheel group membership and sudoers rule granting full admin access
Restarted node1 safely with nohup reboot
Polled until node1 became available post-restart
Confirmed new boot ID: 252e4f5d-cba9-44a5-88dd-205775438dc1 (changed, restart proven)
Verified post-restart: sshd active, opsadmin account and home directory intact, wheel/sudoers config preserved

evidence.requirement: opsadmin account created with home directory and wheel group membership
evidence.summary: useradd created opsadmin (uid=1000) in wheel group; home dir /home/opsadmin exists with drwx------ permissions; /etc/sudoers grants %wheel ALL=(ALL) ALL
Reboot scheduled via nohup; command returned 'reboot scheduled' before disconnect

evidence.requirement: node1 changed boot identity after restart
evidence.summary: New boot ID 252e4f5d-cba9-44a5-88dd-205775438dc1 differs from pre-restart ID, confirming node restarted

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart service and account recovery
evidence.summary: sshd active, opsadmin uid=1000 in wheel group, /home/opsadmin drwx------, %wheel sudoers rule intact — all configuration persisted across reboot
